title: upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 + fused ops + rotary/rope improvements
author: Evan Liu
release_notes: Performance: Upgraded attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused QKV and rotary/rope optimizations. Expected p95 latency reduction and throughput gains for typical generation workloads. Rollout: staged canary, no user-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: improve token latency and throughput across our serving fleet by adopting FlashAttentionV2 kernels plus a set of fused ops and rotary/rope optimizations. This PR replaces the older flash attention wrapper with a robust V2 path that handles variable key/value lengths, supports fused QKV projection when the model layout allows it, and includes a more efficient rotary/rope application that reduces extra memory copies. We also add a runtime feature flag and auto-fallback to the legacy kernels on unsupported GPUs or in case of correctness checks failing at startup. Changes are gated behind a config flag (enable_flashattn_v2) and will be rolled out via canary. Benchmarks: microbenchmarks on A100 and H100 show median token latency improvements of ~12% and p95 improvements of ~15% for generation workloads with sequence lengths in 512-2048; batch=16 throughput improved ~22% in peak scenarios; KV cache resident memory reduced ~9% for 16k tokens due to fused attention buffer reuse and fewer temporary tensors. Compatibility: maintains same API surface and KV cache semantics; we added correctness tests that compare outputs (fp16/fp32/torch.bfloat16) against the legacy path with tolerance levels used in previous attention PRs. Testing: unit tests for fused QKV path, rotary math refactor tests, integration tests exercising streaming and continuous batching, CI perf job updated to include the new kernels. Observability: added kernel-level metrics (attn_kernel_variant, attn_time_ms, attn_temp_memory_bytes) and a per-model knob to opt-out. Rollout plan: 1) merge to main and enable flag default=false; 2) enable canary on 10% of hosted traffic and a subset of Dedicated clusters for 48h; 3) if no regressions, ramp to 50% for 24h then 100% rollout. Relation to prior work: follows up on earlier attention upgrades (see PR-35840, PR-34211, PR-32567) and aligns with ENG-4123 and ENG-4190. Implementation notes: fused QKV assumes contiguous weight layout; when model quantization or packing prevents fusion we fall back to non-fused kernels. The rope/rotary implementation supports several legacy interface variants and is configurable via model metadata. Observed CI: two transient CI flakes on first run (CUDA kernel launch timeout) were fixed by adding a short reinit delay during local GPU testing. Impact: expected to reduce inference cost per token for customers on Dedicated and Hosted and improve tail latency for real-time apps.
commits: Initial FlashAttentionV2 integration and abstraction layer
Add fused QKV projection path and unit tests
Optimize rotary/rope application to avoid extra copies and reduce memory
Add runtime flag and auto-fallback with correctness checks
Metrics and perf CI updates; documentation for rollout

notes: This PR is part of a multi-step effort to modernize attention runtime; monitor attn_kernel_variant and attn_time_ms dashboards during canary. If regressions appear, toggle enable_flashattn_v2=false to rollback the kernel path immediately.
